title: Lincoln Park built on Coleman's old garden square
summary: He locates Lincoln Park on a whole square formerly Coleman's vegetable garden, built about 1905 with a fence and a big dance hall.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now and then, now and then. They didn't start building around that about 1915. I see. Well, we'll start asking about the park, which was right there. Was it, could you tell me where was the park, where the park, Lincoln Park was? Lincoln Park was right there where I lived there by the welfare. And the welfare is then, the whole thing was founded by the Cosset Avenue, Oleander, and Fushet. So it was a one whole block. The whole square. The whole square. I see. The whole square. And do you remember when it was made? I mean, you told me before that it used to be an empty lot. Yeah, that's the old man Coleman, that owned the house. Who? Old man Coleman, Mr. Coleman. How do you spell his name? Coleman. Coleman. Coleman. Coleman. Coleman, yeah. Coleman. Used to own, own the whole square. I see. It had a, it made garden in there. I see. The garden, what do you mean by garden? Very, very, very, very careful. Always vegetable. That was when you were a kid? Yes. I see. And how old were you when, when they made a... The park, that was what they've been, they built that park about 19, 19-5. So you were about 10 years old? About nine years old. Nine years. Nine, ten years old. And when they built the park, what did they make out there? Any fence or...? Oh yeah, they built a big fence all the way around. Fence or...? A boat fence. I see. A feather-age boat fence. I see. And what was in the park? What did they make right in the park? They just built that big, a big dance hall. Big dance hall? Big dance hall. That's when they... They gave shows. Yeah. Every Sunday night, they have a big show. I see. After the show, dance. A big show of dance. And people all over the city. That's the only dance hall they had in the city that died. Only dance hall? No big dance halls. And we had another little dance hall, but they were... Like this guy, this guy was more like a house man. Uh-huh. I see. They had a whole lot of little halls all around the city, but... Not as big as this house, you know. Yeah. Little small places. But this most of the life was out there, man. People would come out and have a... For the woods going up. What you call them? Flying horses. Right. And what store has the... Ferris wheel?
Did they have a ferris wheel somewhere?
